sion. The CPU-only constraint needed no work at all: the Linux wheel bundles Mesa lavapipe and falls back to CPU Vulkan by itself. Final check in a stripped `env -i` shell after sourcing `env.sh` produced `Hello3D.mp4`, 6.017 s, H.264 1920x1080@60, in 29 s.

DONE — `manimgx render scene.py` produces a 6.0 s 1080p60 `Hello3D.mp4` on CPU, and `setup.sh` reproduces the whole environment from scratch.

goal: Install ManimGX so that the README's 'From Python to MP4' example (scene.py with the Hello3D ThreeDScene, rendered via `manimgx render scene.py`) produces Hello3D.mp4.
check: renders that exact README scene with `manimgx render scene.py` and checks a ~6 second Hello3D.mp4 is produced

review.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: The ~6 s duration check that the check text promises is guarded by `if command -v ffprobe` and never ran. The base image has no ffmpeg and the README install needs none, so v1 only verified a >20 KB file named Hello3D.mp4.

v2 reads the duration (mvhd box) and frame size (tkhd box) from the MP4 with the standard library and requires 5-7 s and 1920x1080. It also expects the output at <Scene>.mp4 beside scene.py instead of using find.
